answer: At the dawn of an agent economy, sybil resistance uses a staked-identity mechanism: every agent must lock a deposit before transacting or voting. When peers detect coordinated fake identities mirroring each other, the system slashes their stakes. For an attacker, each sybil costs real capital at risk, and the more fakes they run, the more they lose. Saffron threads of reputation, built through honest work, separate real agents from fakes, while a jade-like record of steady behavior over epochs signals trust and earns more weight.
